column4: Visit note | 2025-07-21 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Rabeya Siddique, 45, female. Mrs. Siddique states she has been feeling restless, struggling with poor sleep, and noticing tense muscles. She mentions these concerns began after witnessing a road accident in Chattogram. She works as a cricket coach and leads an active lifestyle. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. Relevant examination shows no acute distress. On examination: GAD-7 score 18, BP 116/71 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 87 kg. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-07-22 03:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Prosenjit Nath, 64, male. Mr. Nath reports a burning sensation in both feet, numbness in his toes, and tingling like pins and needles. He notes his symptoms became worse since walking barefoot at home in Savar. He works as a tailor, sitting for long hours. He reports no known comorbidities. Examination shows intact cranial nerves and normal reflexes. On examination: reduced sensation at 4 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 111/77 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 81 kg. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-07-26 10:30 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Ziaur Sarkar, 42, male. Mr. Sarkar complains of persistent bloating and stools that switch unpredictably between loose and hard. He states his discomfort became worse since starting a high-pressure job in Khilgaon. He works as a madrasa teacher. He has a known history of Hypothyroidism. Abdominal examination is soft with mild tenderness, no masses felt. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 116/85 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 54 kg. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-07-26 11:00 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Morium Patwary, 58, female. Mrs. Patwary describes knee pain when using stairs, stiffness in the morning lasting for a few minutes, and a noticeable creaking in her knee. She explains the pain became worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Dhanmondi. She works as a homemaker. She has no chronic comorbidities. Examination reveals mild crepitus and restricted terminal flexion. On examination: BMI 30.8, BP 127/76 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 45 kg. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment including a knee X-ray; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-07-26 12:00 PM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Lipi Munshi, 23, female. Miss Munshi presents with bothersome pimples and blackheads on her face, marks left after previous pimples, and spots on her back. She notes her breakout flared after using a heavy face cream bought in Mohammadpur. She works as a graphic designer. She has a history of Essential hypertension. Skin inspection shows no cystic lesions. On examination: about 9 inflamed spots on the face, BP 145/90 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 72 kg. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and avoid squeezing spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-07-28 09:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Liton Awal, 25, male. Mr. Awal attends for a review regarding marks left after pimples and spots on his back. He mentions his skin condition became worse since working in a hot kitchen in Mirpur. He works as a security guard. He has a history of Hypothyroidism. Examination shows stable skin lesions with few active papules. On examination: about 9 inflamed spots on the face, BP 119/81 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 63 kg. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: chronic follow-up; continue current measures, and no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and avoid squeezing spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-07-29 11:30 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Shampa Bose, 37, female. Mrs. Bose complains of itchy dry patches on her elbows and knees, noting her symptoms are always worse in winter. She explains her condition flared during the dry winter in Lalbagh. She works as a farmer. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. Skin exam reveals scaly erythematous plaques. On examination: affected area about 8 cm across, BP 121/77 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 66 kg. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-07-29 04:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Salma Majumder, 37, female. Mrs. Majumder describes a throbbing headache on one side accompanied by light hurting her eyes. She reports unusual atypical presentation with flashing zigzag lights before the attacks and tingling in one hand, and notes attacks are triggered by skipping meals while travelling in Kamrangirchar. She works as a schoolteacher. She has no chronic comorbidities. Neurological examination is otherwise normal. On examination: about 7 headache days a month, BP 136/70 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 64 kg. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-07-30 09:00 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Mala Halder, 47, female. Mrs. Halder reports a persistent runny nose, itchy eyes, and frequent sneezing fits. She states her symptoms flare each spring in Bogura. She works as a delivery rider. She has no documented comorbidities. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy. On examination: about 14 sneezing fits a day, BP 131/83 mmHg, pulse 85 bpm, weight 92 kg. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-07-30 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Abdul Majumder, 35, male. Mr. Majumder reports no specific complaints of his own but noted a high reading on a pharmacy machine. He presents with an atypical presentation of nosebleeds and blurred vision with no headache, which was found during a free health camp in Tongi. He works as an NGO field officer. He has no chronic comorbidities. Cardiovascular exam shows normal rhythm. On examination: BP 160/96 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 56 kg. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-07-31 03:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Faruk Alam, 40, male. Mr. Alam looks noticeably pale, experiences breathlessness on the stairs, and suffers from constant tiredness. He mentions this started after months of skipping lunch during long shifts in Sirajganj. He works as an NGO field officer. He has a background of Essential hypertension. Conjunctiva are pale. On examination: haemoglobin 8.6 g/dL, BP 142/93 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 93 kg. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed at this stage. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.
